headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and cascading errors; prompt injection is moderate, while compliance risk is limited by the profiles provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads files and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context”; Agent B reads/writes files and consumes stdin/stdout plus APIs. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if A’s outputs land in files or streams B parses as trusted content. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF A’s generated files are fed into B’s stdin/stdout or file inputs without sanitization
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a strict content/schema separator for inter-agent files
Prefix all handoff artifacts with machine-readable provenance metadata
Review B prompts/parsers for instruction-following on file content
Use a dedicated handoff directory with read-only permissions for B
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing and taint tracking

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing and product-marketing context, while B touches datasets, models, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files and handles hub/sdk tokens. Both have filesystem access and allowlisted egress, so a shared workspace could expose A’s content to B’s broader data surfaces or outbound APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A and B share any writable directory or mounted workspace
IF B ingests A-produced files into logs, datasets, or API calls
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points for A and B
Store secrets for B outside any shared directory
Disable automatic upload of local files in B workflows
Quickly audit recent files in shared paths for sensitive marketing context
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; A also supports multiple instances, while B’s concurrency scope is not stated and it cannot modify git state. If they share a directory, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite each other’s outputs by default. Because locking/isolation is not documented, uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same directory or file set
IF no external lock or per-agent workspace is enforced
mitigations: Assign separate output directories to each agent
Use file locks around any shared artifacts
Run one agent at a time for shared resources
Check for overlapping temp paths before execution
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and namespace isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: A’s marketing outputs can become inputs to B’s CLI/Python workflows, and B can act on files, logs, and configuration data. If B treats A’s text as authoritative, a bad claim or malformed instruction can cascade into downstream artifacts or actions. The profiles do not show explicit verification between them, so the pathway exists but is not proven dangerous by default.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s output without a validation step
IF A’s generated text is used to create configs, prompts, or commands
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based review step before B consumes A output
Require B to validate schemas and reject free-form instructions
Keep A outputs in a read-only staging area
Log and diff A-to-B handoffs for quick inspection
requires-engineering: implement automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: A is a marketing agent touching marketing content and product marketing context; B handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, configuration files, and secrets, with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, but the mixed data classes and token handling create a plausible retention/logging mismatch if the same data flows through both. No direct jurisdiction mismatch is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated or customer data is routed through both agents
IF B logs or retains A-origin content longer than A’s policy allows
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for B logs and outputs
Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Document which data classes each agent may process
Delete any shared artifacts after the run
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both agents
